data.name: Draw secondaries
data.answer: No. Follow your chosen mission pack and its Fixed/Tactical rules.
data.summary: If you are using Tactical Secondary Missions, draw the Secondary Mission cards required by your mission pack at the start of your Command phase, then resolve any When Drawn instructions. Check retained cards, draw limits and any mission-specific exceptions. If you are using Fixed Missions, keep your chosen missions instead of drawing new ones.
data.question: Should you draw new cards while using Fixed Missions?
conditions: This is a reminder to use your mission deck; it does not draw cards or track your active missions.
The number of cards drawn and whether you retain or refill cards depend on the mission pack you are playing.
data.targetText: You, when using Tactical Secondary Missions at the start of your Command phase. Follow your selected mission pack.

data.why: Keep the rules attached to the unit and the actual event, rather than splitting one activation across generic screens.
data.body: Keep these cards beside your charge decisions. Check the relevant unit’s conditions without selecting it in the app.
data.title: Charge Moves
data.answer: After resolving the current unit’s legal sequence and immediate effects. End-of-phase rules still wait until the phase closes.
data.question: When should you select another unit?

data.why: In this edition, the detailed charge-target selection belongs to making the move after the roll.
data.body: Choose a unit that can declare a charge and has not done so this phase. General restrictions include being engaged, having Advanced or Fallen Back, or lacking an enemy within 12 inches. Roll 2D6 to establish the maximum charge-move distance.
data.title: Charge Rolls
data.answer: No. The unit must first be eligible to declare the charge. A specific rule may create an exception, but the dice alone do not.
data.question: Does a high roll cancel an eligibility restriction?

data.why: The next phase begins with its own pile-in step, before units are selected to fight.
data.body: Resolve end-of-Charge rules. Notice which units actually completed charge moves and what effects carry into Fight.
data.title: End of Charge
data.answer: No. The charge-move rule grants it after the move. Distinguish a declaration, a roll, and a completed legal move.
data.question: Does declaring a charge alone grant Fights First?

data.why: A distance that looks sufficient may still fail because no legal final position exists.
data.body: For the charge move, select targets within both 12 inches and the rolled maximum distance. The final position must engage every charge target and no non-target enemy unit. Check model-level movement requirements and coherency.
data.title: Charge Moves
data.answer: The charge is resolved without that move. You may also choose not to make the move. A completed charge grants Fights First until the turn ends.
data.question: What if a legal charge move is impossible?

data.why: Start with the timing window before choosing a charging unit.
data.body: Resolve rules triggered at the start of the active player’s Charge phase.
data.title: Start of Charge
data.answer: Check the unit’s movement and any restrictions still lasting this turn. Your Banshees’ exception does not remove unrelated restrictions.
data.question: Did an earlier move or ability prevent a charge?

data.why: A heading saying “Command” is not enough; the ability’s wording determines its place.
data.body: Now resolve rules triggered in the Command phase that do not belong to a specific start, end, Core CP, or Battle-shock window.
data.title: Command Abilities
data.answer: No. Keep specific triggers in their own windows. Optional choices need their conditions and eligible targets checked before you use them.
data.question: Should you resolve a start-of-phase rule here?

data.why: Separate Core CP from additional CP awarded by an army rule.
data.body: Each player gains one Core Command Point, even though only one player is taking this turn.
data.title: Gain Command Points
data.answer: Yes. Both players gain the Core CP in each Command phase. This screen teaches the step; it does not keep a CP balance.
data.question: Does the opponent gain this CP too?

data.why: Mission instructions come after the other end-of-phase rules in this sequence.
data.body: Resolve end-of-Command-phase rules other than mission rules first. Then consult the mission for anything achieved or triggered at this point.
data.title: End of Command
data.answer: At the mission’s specified timing. This app does not infer a mission or calculate score; consult the pack you are playing.
data.question: When do you consult scoring instructions?

data.why: Do not automatically clear Battle-shock at the start of the turn. The 11th-edition test includes units exactly at half-strength.
data.body: The active player checks units that are already battle-shocked or at or below half-strength. Roll 2D6 against an applicable Leadership value; meeting or exceeding it succeeds. A unit already battle-shocked recovers here if its roll succeeds.
data.title: Battle-shock
data.answer: Yes: it is at or below half-strength. Attached units use the appropriate starting-strength rules; do not treat a surviving leader as a fresh unit without checking them.
data.question: A five-model unit has two models left. Must you check it?

data.why: Timing words matter: “at the start” happens before gaining Core CP.
data.body: Resolve rules triggered at the start of the active player’s Command phase. This is a separate window from the later Command Abilities step.
data.title: Start of Command
data.answer: In this opening window, before the Core CP step. Check whether the ability applies in your turn, the opponent’s turn, or both.
data.question: Where does a start-of-phase ability belong?

data.why: Do not replace this with a blanket “the non-active player always picks first” rule.
data.body: Begin Fights First selections with the active player and alternate eligible units. When that group is exhausted, the player who moves the sequence into Remaining Combats makes the next selection. Alternate until eligible fights are resolved; return to Fights First if an eligible Fights First unit appears.
data.title: Unit Fights
data.answer: It depends on who transitions the sequence out of Fights First. Follow section 12.04 rather than assuming a fixed player. Select a legal normal or overrun fight type for the chosen unit.
data.question: Who gets the next remaining-combat choice?

data.why: An engaging consolidation can give an enemy that has not fought a new opportunity to fight.
data.body: After the Fight step, the active player resolves their chosen eligible consolidation moves, then the opponent. Select the required consolidation mode based on engagement, nearby enemies, or objectives, and check its conditions.
data.title: Consolidate
data.answer: No. The applicable mode has priority and restrictions. If you engage an enemy that has not fought, follow the extra fight instructions before continuing.
data.question: Is consolidation always a free move toward an objective?

data.why: Some effects last a phase, others a turn or until a later Command phase.
data.body: Resolve the end-of-Fight window. Check remaining end-of-turn rules in their own window before passing the turn.
data.title: End of Fight
data.answer: No. Read each effect’s duration. End of Fight and end of turn are distinct triggers; do not expire a longer effect early.
data.question: Does every buff disappear at this point?

data.why: Do not insert a routine pile-in before every selected unit fights: this edition has a separate pile-in step.
data.body: The active player resolves the optional pile-in moves they choose with eligible units, then the other player does so. A unit may make no more than one pile-in move in this step. Check the full target and positioning requirements.
data.title: Pile In
data.answer: No. Models in base contact cannot move, and the move has target, closer-to, engagement, and coherency conditions. Some abilities modify the distance but not every restriction.
data.question: Can every model in an eligible unit freely move 3 inches?

data.why: Do not replace this with a blanket “the non-active player always picks first” rule.
data.body: Begin Fights First selections with the active player and alternate eligible units. When that group is exhausted, the player who moves the sequence into Remaining Combats makes the next selection. Alternate until eligible fights are resolved; return to Fights First if an eligible Fights First unit appears.
data.title: Fight
data.answer: It depends on who transitions the sequence out of Fights First. Follow section 12.04 rather than assuming a fixed player. Select a legal normal or overrun fight type for the chosen unit.
data.question: Who gets the next remaining-combat choice?

data.why: The opponent’s turn does not mean your engaged units are inactive.
data.body: Both armies participate in this phase. Resolve start-of-Fight rules before the separate pile-in step.
data.title: Start of Fight
data.answer: No. Both players resolve eligible units, subject to the current sequence and any relevant exceptions.
data.question: Are you only watching during the opponent’s Fight phase?

data.why: Keep the rules attached to the unit and the actual event, rather than splitting one activation across generic screens.
data.body: Scan your shared movement options and the units with relevant abilities below. Resolve moves in any legal order; there is no unit checklist to complete.
data.title: Move Units
data.answer: After resolving the current unit’s legal sequence and immediate effects. End-of-phase rules still wait until the phase closes.
data.question: When should you select another unit?

data.why: The order of a transport’s move and its passengers’ move can change their options.
data.body: Disembark and ingress are move types in this edition, not a generic extra movement step after all other movement. Check their own eligibility and setup restrictions.
data.title: Transports & Reserves
data.answer: No. Rapid, tactical, and combat disembark modes have different consequences. Review section 18.04 before making the choice. Reserve arrival also needs its permitted round and placement checked.
data.question: Can you assume every disembarking unit may charge?

data.why: This is where a pending effect or a target choice may matter to the rest of your turn.
data.body: After the move selections are complete, resolve rules triggered at the end of the Movement phase.
data.title: End of Movement
data.answer: Check any ability used earlier for an end-of-phase instruction. Also check for fresh choices whose trigger is specifically the end of Movement.
data.question: Did an earlier choice leave a consequence to resolve now?

data.why: Movement is not just choosing the models you want to push forward.
data.body: Select an unselected friendly unit, including units in reserve or embarked in a transport, then choose a legal move type. Repeat until every unit has been selected—even units that remain stationary.
data.title: Unit Movement
data.answer: Yes. Remain stationary is a choice in the sequence. For other units, check normal, advance, fall-back, disembark, and ingress eligibility.
data.question: Does an unmoving unit still need to be selected?

data.why: Opening triggers cannot be saved for an arbitrary point later in the phase.
data.body: Resolve rules triggered at the start of the active player’s Movement phase before selecting units to move.
data.title: Start of Movement
data.answer: Check explicit start-of-phase wording. Movement-triggered abilities wait for their own selection, setup, or move-end event.
data.question: What needs to happen before the first unit moves?

data.why: Keep the rules attached to the unit and the actual event, rather than splitting one activation across generic screens.
data.body: The opponent resolves one unit at a time. Your shared responses and affected-unit reminders are visible together below; this does not activate your army in place of theirs.
data.title: Opponent’s Movement
data.answer: After resolving the current unit’s legal sequence and immediate effects. End-of-phase rules still wait until the phase closes.
data.question: When should you select another unit?

data.why: Keep the rules attached to the unit and the actual event, rather than splitting one activation across generic screens.
data.body: The opponent resolves one unit at a time. Your shared responses and affected-unit reminders are visible together below; this does not activate your army in place of theirs.
data.title: Opponent’s Shooting
data.answer: After resolving the current unit’s legal sequence and immediate effects. End-of-phase rules still wait until the phase closes.
data.question: When should you select another unit?

data.why: A round contains one turn for each player; do not advance the round number after only the first turn.
data.body: After the second player’s turn, resolve end-of-round rules other than mission rules first, then the mission’s end-of-round instructions. Check whether the mission ends the battle before beginning another round.
data.title: End of Battle Round
data.answer: No. Follow your mission. Continue only if another battle round should be played.
data.question: Does this app decide when the battle ends?

data.why: The mission establishes the first player, who remains first in each round. Set that choice in session details.
data.body: Before either player begins their turn, resolve rules triggered at the start of the battle round. Then the first player takes their turn.
data.title: Start of Battle Round
data.answer: No. It happens once per battle round, before the first turn.
data.question: Does this opening repeat before both players’ turns?

data.why: Keep the rules attached to the unit and the actual event, rather than splitting one activation across generic screens.
data.body: Scan the unit cards as your army shoots. Setup shooters appear early because their effects may help later units. You choose the legal order.
data.title: Unit Shooting
data.answer: After resolving the current unit’s legal sequence and immediate effects. End-of-phase rules still wait until the phase closes.
data.question: When should you select another unit?

data.why: Ordering matters for the Falcon and War Walkers in your roster.
data.body: Resolve effects triggered by that unit’s completed shooting before choosing the next unit. Repeat the selection and attacks sequence for the units you choose to shoot with.
data.title: After Shooting
data.answer: Possibly: check whether it hit a qualifying target and whether the later unit meets the benefit’s conditions. The army reminders below explain the roster-specific checks.
data.question: Could an earlier shooter help a later unit?

data.why: A unit-level reminder does not establish that every model or weapon is eligible.
data.body: Check range, visibility, and target restrictions for each selected weapon. Resolve attacks using the current attack sequence and the selected weapon’s characteristics.
data.title: Attacks
data.answer: Only if that target satisfies the rule’s keywords and other conditions. Read the attack’s target, not just its expected damage.
data.question: Does a bonus against vehicles apply to a different target?

data.why: “After a unit shoots” and “end of phase” do not mean the same thing.
data.body: Resolve rules that explicitly trigger at the end of the Shooting phase. Review any effects that expire now before entering Charge.
data.title: End of Shooting
data.answer: Do not assume so. Resolve each ability in its specified window, and check the rules for simultaneous triggers where necessary.
data.question: Can you delay a just-after-shooting trigger until now?

data.why: Do not apply an old-edition exception by memory. The shooting type determines the rules.
data.body: Select an eligible unit that has not shot this phase. Check whether normal, assault, close-quarters, or indirect shooting is permitted. An Advance normally restricts you to eligible Assault weapons.
data.title: Unit Shooting
data.answer: Check assault-shooting eligibility and its Assault weapons. Also consider any special rule that changes the general restrictions. Fall-back consequences must be checked separately.
data.question: What should you check for a unit that Advanced?

data.why: Before-shooting and after-shooting abilities are different windows.
data.body: Resolve rules triggered at the start of the active player’s Shooting phase.
data.title: Start of Shooting
data.answer: No. Look for its exact trigger. Some choices must be made before selecting a unit; others happen only after attacks resolve.
data.question: Must every ability usable in this phase happen now?

data.why: End of Fight and end of turn are separate windows.
data.body: After Fight has ended, resolve end-of-turn rules other than mission rules first, then resolve the mission’s end-of-turn instructions.
data.title: End of Turn
data.answer: No. Read its actual expiry. Consult the mission for its own triggers; this app does not decide whether the battle has ended.
data.question: Should you clear an effect lasting until your next Command phase now?

data.why: This walkthrough includes the opening windows here so they are not forgotten.
data.body: Before entering Command, resolve rules triggered at the start of this player’s turn. Start of turn and start of Command are separate windows.
data.title: Start of Turn
data.answer: No. A turn has a start step, five phases, and an end step. Follow each rule’s timing.
data.question: Is start of turn the same as start of Command?
